evidence: The Roman Conquest of Italy, Le patronat judiciaire, Rhetoric and Public Life and the other Roman studies are Jean-Michel David's, approximately 26–27 of 33 listed thesis-work citations. The Postmodernist Turn and The New Humanism are Hoeveler's (5); Cognitive Distortions, Humor Styles, and Depression is by Rnic, Dozois and Martin (1).

Gandhian Utopia, Recapturing Anthropology, Lions of the Punjab and the related anthropology titles belong to Richard Gabriel Fox, approximately 14 of 23 listed thesis-work citations. The Long March and Brill's Companion to Ancient Macedon belong to Robin Lane Fox (4). Other unrelated and fragmentary records prevent a secure two-thirds-dominant assignment; this is a substantial mixture.

The Myth of Continents (21), Dividing the Ocean Sea (4), Wagering the Land and the other geography records account for approximately 29 of 38 listed thesis-work citations to Martin W. Lewis. One Hundred Million Frenchmen (7) is explicitly credited to Martin Deming Lewis, who also wrote Lumberman from Flint; the 1962 journal-only fragment likely repeats his article.

Only Howard Carter: The Path to Tutankhamun and Pharaoh's People are T. G. H. James's (2 of 27 listed thesis-work citations). Three Years Among the Indians and Mexicans (7) is General Thomas James's; The Palaces of Medieval England (3) is Thomas Beaumont James's; Law and the Shaping of Public Education (2) has the education historian Thomas James; The Age of Majority (2) is by T. E. James.

Nearly all the listed weight (37 of 38 thesis-work citations) is James Weldon Johnson's: Black Manhattan, Along This Way, the poetry and spiritual anthologies, God's Trombones, Autobiography of an Ex-Colored Man and his collected writings. The isolated Chronological Writing: Its Concepts and Development (1962; 1) is by James William Johnson.

Urban Disorder and the Shape of Belief (19), The Plan of Chicago (7) and City Water, City Life (7) are the Northwestern historian Carl S. Smith's: at least 33 of 39 listed thesis-work citations. The German-Speaking Community in Hong Kong and A Sense of History belong to Carl T. Smith (3); the recording and Gettysburg records add other contamination. The San Francisco subtitle attached to Urban Disorder is corrupt.

The key is education historian Robert D. Anderson: European Universities, British Universities, University History Teaching, Ceremony in Context and the education records contribute approximately 15 of 28 listed thesis-work citations. Sidelights on the Home Rule Movement and The Lighter Side of My Official Life are Sir Robert Anderson's (5); Vision of the Disinherited is Robert Mapes Anderson's (2), with further namesakes elsewhere. The split does not establish the brief's two-thirds dominance.

Remembering the Year of the French (8), Forgetful Remembrance (5), Between Trauma and Triumphalism (3), Disremembering 1798? (2), Commemorative Heritage (1) and the Great Flu article (1) are Guy Beiner's: 20 of 35 listed thesis-work citations. Ronald Beiner's citizenship, nationalism, political philosophy and Arendt titles account for the remaining approximately 15.

Tertullian, Heresy and Schism According to Cyprian and the other identifiable patristic studies contribute 11 of 24 listed thesis-work citations to Geoffrey D. Dunn; the Church History fragment plausibly adds 1. Imagining the Congo, Introduction: Africa and International Relations Theory, African Guerrillas and Lights...Camera...Africa are Kevin Dunn's (10), alongside unrelated clinical and learning-style fragments (2). Approximately even mixture; neither dominance nor minority is secure.

Creating Abundance and the agricultural, animal-disease and economic-history titles belong to Alan L. Olmstead, usually with Paul W. Rhode (30 of 35 listed thesis-work citations). History of the Persian Empire (2), Assyrian Historiography (1), Tiglath-Pileser I and His Wars (1) and Babylonia as an Assyrian Dependency (1) belong to A. T. Olmstead, the ancient Near Eastern historian.
